chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife while she was pregnant, then he claimed her child after she had given birth, and asserted that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is returned to him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an if the wife is pregnant and the husband later claims the child?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies that once the li'an ceremony is completed, the husband's subsequent claim of paternity does not invalidate the established legal status, nor does it incur the li'an-specific flogging penalty. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that li'an serves as a definitive proof of non-paternity, allowing for the attribution of lineage to the husband if he later asserts it, while distinguishing the procedural penalty from the substantive ruling.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who cursed his wife and she was pregnant. Then he claimed her child after she had given birth, and claimed that it was from him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The child would be returned to him, and he would not be whipped, because the cursing had passed’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who goes through the process of al-Li ‘an (condemnation) against his wife who is pregnant, then claims her child to be his child after childbirth thinking that the child is his. He (the Imam) said, ‘The child can be given to him without whipping because al-Li‘an (condemnation) has become a matter of the past in the case.’”
